contradiction_resolution: No contradiction is recorded: FND-0132 has an empty contradicts_claim_ids list and is compatible with the curated campaign claims. Primary sources support both links in the argument: étale monodromy orbits classify connected components, while connected finite étale covers of normal integral bases are integral. Hartshorne, Exercise III.10.6 supplies the required failure over a nonnormal nodal cubic: a connected degree-two finite étale cover is reducible with two irreducible components. The finding is complementary to FND-0064, FND-0075, FND-0053, FND-0087, FND-0127, and FND-0086, none of which states this normality obstruction. No merge is warranted.

scope.audit_limit: ATT-0082, REV-0133, CLM-0082-2, and CLM-0082-3 were not present as standalone records in the curated claims, sources, or findings files. Promotion therefore validates the stated monodromy-to-irreducibility obstruction and its conditional consequence for any use of the [S_6:H_V] formula, not the full unstated contents of those attempt-local claims.
scope.mathematical_scope: For a finite étale S_6-torsor over a connected locally Noetherian scheme V, π_1^ét(V)-orbits on a geometric fibre classify connected components. If V is normal, then V is integral and every connected component of the torsor is integral, so the orbit count [S_6:H_V] also counts irreducible components. Without normality or another sufficient irreducibility hypothesis, this upgrade is invalid: connected reducible finite étale covers exist over connected nonnormal Noetherian schemes.
scope.precision: Normality is sufficient and load-bearing for the argument recorded in ATT-0082, but it is not logically necessary in every possible replacement argument; integral geometrically unibranch hypotheses or a direct irreducibility proof can suffice. Normality alone also does not imply geometric irreducibility after arbitrary ground-field extension.
